analysis: Mendeley-only biomass transport stress diagnostics; fixed OLS and fixed grouping, no model selection

epistemicStatus.interpretation: All outcomes in this Mendeley cohort have been inspected in prior analyses. These are sensitivity and transport diagnostics on development data, not independent validation, and cannot promote a model or establish generalization beyond these two farms.

input.grouping: 13 connected farm/field components; field aliases with any exact shared farm-coordinate are joined; repeat campaigns at each point stay together for spatial folds.
input.cohortFilter: Retain rows with nonmissing sward_height_cm, target, farm, field_code, campaign, management_type, and coordinates; this yields the 234 height-complete rows in the already frozen biomass development cohort.

leaveOneFarmOut.method: Hold out each entire farm, train on the other farm; score both folds separately and pooled.
leaveOneFarmOut.warning: Only two farms. Results are descriptive case comparisons and do not support farm-population inference.

leaveOneCampaignOut.method: For each campaign, test all rows from that campaign; train on the other campaign only after excluding every row whose (farm, exact latitude, exact longitude) occurs in the test campaign. This prevents spatial point identity crossing the split.
leaveOneCampaignOut.warning: Only two campaigns and repeated locations. This estimates temporal/campaign transfer conditional on non-overlapping sampled points, not general year performance.

spatialBufferSensitivity.method: Fixed LinearRegression with intercept, one predictor sward_height_cm, on the existing 13 leave-one-connected-spatial-component-out folds. For each held-out block, discard training coordinate groups closer than the fixed distance to any held-out coordinate.
spatialBufferSensitivity.zeroDistanceRule: Other components are retained at distance >= 0; held-out component and its repeated campaign rows are always excluded.

subgroupAndSupportDiagnostics.method: For farm, campaign, and management_type, report row count, spatial-block count where applicable, OOF MAE/RMSE/signed bias. Per fold report training and test height ranges, test rows outside training min-max support, and error for in-support versus out-of-support rows.
subgroupAndSupportDiagnostics.supportDefinition: A test height is in support only if it lies within the minimum and maximum training height in that fold; this is a descriptive range check, not a causal explanation.

blockBootstrap.method: 10,000 bootstrap resamples with replacement of the 13 existing 100m spatial-block MAE scores, resampling whole blocks and never rows.
blockBootstrap.warning: Descriptive stability summary only. The 13 blocks are nested within only two farms; bootstrap quantiles are not a population confidence interval.

estimator.definition: sklearn LinearRegression(fit_intercept=true), target kg DM/ha, predictor sward_height_cm only
estimator.featureProcessing: No transformation, imputation, clipping, or scaling; each fold fit uses only its training rows.

runtime: Record aggregate and per-fold CPU fit/predict wall time with perf_counter; report estimator and row counts. Timings are descriptive for this environment.
stopRules: Abort on checksum mismatch, unexpected source or eligible cohort row/group counts, missing required grouping/target values, or non-finite feature/target values.
Do not alter field-component definitions, distance thresholds, candidate, or subgroup definitions after seeing target errors.
Keep every preregistered fold in outputs; if no usable training rows exist, report it as unscored and lower coverage rather than relaxing the split.
interpretationLimits: Mendeley outcomes were already reviewed; none of these results are pristine validation.
The 13 spatial components are nested in two farms and the two campaigns; no population-level uncertainty is claimed.
Height and biomass are observed at the same sampling points, and measurement order relative to clipping is undocumented.
A train-range support flag does not isolate extrapolation from farm, campaign, or management shifts.
No Dryad rows, predictions, metrics, or outcomes may be read by this experiment.
